best_for: Office and IT staff who sign in to Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop or Dev Box with a work account, and Mac users who need to reach a Windows PC by Remote Desktop.

points.title: A client for Microsoft's cloud PCs
points.text: Windows App opens Cloud PCs, Azure Virtual Desktop, Dev Box and remote PCs from one home screen, where you can pin the ones you use most and switch between several accounts.

points.title: Work accounts only
points.text: Signing in needs a work or school account from your administrator; a personal Microsoft account does not work. You can skip sign-in to connect straight to a remote PC on platforms that support it.

points.title: Remote Desktop Services: not on Windows
points.text: On Windows, the app cannot reach Remote Desktop Services, and Microsoft points those users to the older Remote Desktop app. On a Mac it does connect to Remote Desktop Services, so the Windows and Mac versions are not the same.

points.title: It does not include the service
points.text: The app is free, but it only connects. Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop and Dev Box are paid services your organization has to provide.

points.title: Remote session features
points.text: It handles multiple monitors, dynamic resolution, redirection of webcams, audio, drives and printers, and Teams optimizations inside the remote session.

points.title: Mac needs a recent macOS
points.text: The macOS package listed here is a universal installer that declares macOS 15 as its minimum, and Microsoft's release notes say macOS 13 stopped getting updates in April 2026. On Windows, the MSIX builds cover x86, x64 and Arm64 on Windows 10 1809 or later.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 36 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so an older Mac build needs another source.
